turns.assessment: The first physical signature is complete loss of input and output power across the S06→S19 amplifier chain, including loss at the booster input, while every amplifier's pump-current telemetry remained unchanged. This localizes the interruption ahead of the booster at the OMS input patch, rather than to a span or amplifier. The hard all-channel loss and recent maintenance at S06 strongly indicate a disconnected or broken patch cord.

proposals.rationale: A pulled input patch at oms.S06-S19 would remove all channels before amp0, exactly matching lost input/output power throughout the chain and the downstream OCH LOS and service failures. Unchanged pump currents exclude amplifier pump failures, and recent S06 maintenance supports accidental patch disturbance.

Failure of the S06 WSS port feeding this degree could also suppress all channels before the booster, but there is no direct ROADM equipment alarm and the maintenance-associated hard patch loss is more likely.
Contamination at the same patch is maintenance-related, but normally causes reduced power rather than the observed complete signal loss.
